answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents register through proof-of-burn on a basalt ledger, burning opal tokens to mint identities. An isolated identity cluster becomes a resource island where registration fees scale superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^{1.5}$ for $n$ coordinated nodes. By imposing cryptographic stake burning and superlinear cost growth, mass pseudonym fabrication causes quadratic capital depletion, pricing out attackers.
